decision: Qualify automatic lease maintenance across a real OS-process boundary with a competing coordinator process and a crash/reclaim control.
problem: WorkerRuntime automatic heartbeat was covered inside one Node process, but Slice 1 lacked evidence that a long-running worker keeps a fenced lease against an independent process, and that authority becomes reclaimable after the worker process dies and heartbeats stop.

reviews.correctness: Preferred a spawned WorkerRuntime using the production MissionQueueStore/Coordinator contract, then a separate spawned contender after the original lease duration. This tests the exact lease-token and durable-store semantics needed before qrexec process boundaries.
reviews.robustness_security: Preferred a crash control that SIGKILLs the worker process, waits beyond the bounded lease window, and requires a separate process to reclaim. Healthy-heartbeat contention must return no mission; stale ownership after crash must not remain indefinitely.
reviews.latency_resources_regression: Preferred two short deterministic process-boundary tests over a daemon, external scheduler, or Qubes dependency. The tests add no production traffic or runtime state and reuse the existing process worker harness.

alternatives_rejected: In-process timer tests only: validate heartbeat code but not persistence/reload behavior across process boundaries.
Very long leases instead of automatic heartbeats: reduce renewal traffic but materially slow crash recovery and stale-owner reclamation.
Start Slice 2 qrexec testing immediately: higher fidelity, but it would mix transport failures with an unqualified Mission/runtime lease-liveness contract.
qa: A spawned long-running worker remains authoritative beyond the original lease duration while automatic heartbeats succeed.
A separate spawned contender cannot reclaim the healthy worker's mission.
After SIGKILL, heartbeats stop and the same mission becomes reclaimable only after lease expiry.
The healthy path ends in exactly one durable completed mission.
failure_lessons: Per-claim fencing prevents stale terminal writes, but without process-boundary lease-liveness evidence it does not prove a real worker can safely execute tasks longer than one lease.
Crash recovery and healthy-heartbeat protection are complementary requirements: a lease must neither expire too early nor remain owned forever.
remaining_gate: Run the new process-boundary heartbeat campaign green under test:mission-runtime on the exact head, then keep Slice 1 frozen before extracting Qubes transport/qualification.
